factual_errors.claim: The internal channels are dispatched via ipcMain.emit inside WindowManager, App and DataCenter (windowManager.ts:369-495, app/index.ts:668-765, dataCenter/index.ts:107/117/136)
factual_errors.repository_evidence: packages/desktop/src/main/app/windowManager.ts:367-495 and app/index.ts:658-765 are _listenForIpcMain subscriber bodies (ipcMain.on / onInternalChannel), not emit sites; only dataCenter/index.ts:107/117/136 are ipcMain.emit. Actual emit sites are windows/editor.ts:396-536, menu/actions/*.ts, preferences/index.ts:137, dataCenter/index.ts:107/117/136, app/index.ts:807
factual_errors.explanation: Two of the three cited line ranges are subscription code, not dispatch code, so the 'who dispatches' attribution is partly wrong; the underlying fact that ipcMain.emit is used as an in-process bus is correct and the recommendation does not rest on the misattribution

rationale: The answer is a thorough, evidence-backed architecture review. It correctly identifies the current desktop platform (Electron ~42.1.0 sandboxed app in packages/desktop, @muyajs/core as the live engine, legacy @marktext/muyajs retired) and treats legacy platforms and stale docs as historical rather than current. Nearly all claims are verified against implementation, config, tests, and package metadata with accurate paths and line numbers; the review explicitly separates current evidence from documentation intent. It explains where changes spread (scattered IPC handlers, sender-reflection window identity, dual-engine declaration, save/export living in menu actions), gives three option sets each including status quo with explicit quality-attribute trade-offs, cost, risk, rollback, and consequences of inaction, and derives recommendations from verified evidence (the file.ts TODO, existing TypedEmitter, @muyajs/core API churn). The migration plan is incremental, reversible, and gated by named unit/e2e specs. Four minor factual imprecisions (dispatch vs subscribe attribution, scatter undercount, conformance-percentage file attribution, detached-HEAD description) do not affect any recommendation; there are no material errors and no unresolved decision-relevant conflicts, so the accuracy gate passes. All nine dimensions earn full credit; total 18/18.
